headline: KSE-100 slides 0.96% as US-Iran tensions and a hot CPI print box in the SBP — refineries and cash-rich banks stay the desk's shelter of choice.
summary: KSE-100 closed at 174,776.60 today, down 0.96% — its second straight sharp down day — as US-Iran tensions keep Brent near $94. Layered on top: August CPI hit 11.1%, more than triple last year's rate, which all but kills hopes of an SBP rate cut at the September 14 meeting. The desk is reading this as risk-off: favouring refineries riding the crude move and large, well-capitalized banks locking in high T-bill/PIB yields, while avoiding OMCs, autos, cement and power names squeezed by costs and the unresolved circular-debt problem. Stick with cheap valuations and dated catalysts; skip broad index-chasing.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: Brent at $94.28 lifts crack-spread expectations, and a pending refinery-upgrade policy tailwind makes this a narrower, more defensible way to play the oil move than OMCs or broad E&P (per macro.json sector_tilt).

sectors.name: Banks (large-cap)
sectors.why: The confirmed 11.1% August CPI print removes near-term rate-cut risk into the Sept 14 MPC, which reinforces rather than undercuts the T-bill/PIB carry income large, well-capitalized banks are earning (6M bills at 11.80%, 10Y PIBs at 12.30%).

sectors.name: Oil & Gas E&P
sectors.why: Elevated crude is a real tailwind (georisk.json flags OGDC/PPL/MARI as beneficiaries of the energy shock), but that same shock is stress-scored 74/100 on the desk's own geo-risk radar and is what's dragging the index down today — a tailwind wrapped in real conflict risk, not a clean call.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: Squeezed between a near-daily-reset pump price and the rising import cost of the fuel itself (macro.json sector_tilt).

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Rate-sensitive and import-cost exposed just as the CPI shock pushes any SBP relief further out.

sectors.name: Cement & Power/IPPs
sectors.why: Same rate-sensitivity as autos, plus power/IPPs carry the added overhang of unresolved circular debt heading into the IMF's September review.

Fundamentals price it cheap too (P/E 7.13, cheapest third of PSX).

watchlist.risk: Mid-cap with a beta of 1.2 — moves more than the market, which cuts both ways in a risk-off tape. No live technical trigger is firing today; this is a fundamentals-and-catalyst case, not a momentum one.

watchlist.angle: Sits in the desk's favoured refinery trade (crack-spread tailwind from Brent near $94) and the chart backs it up — close near 1,167.52, above both the 20- and 50-day averages, RSI 67.7, only 2.6% off its 20-day high, with a 1.39x volume surge. Cheap on paper (P/E 4.9, forward P/E 3.45) with a confirmed dividend landing 2026-10-12.

The chart is constructive too — above both moving averages, RSI 62.7, only 2.5% off its 20-day high. E&P benefits directly from Brent near $94; georisk.json names E&P peers OGDC/PPL/MARI as beneficiaries of the same energy shock.
watchlist.risk: The same energy shock driving today's -0.96% KSE-100 close is what's lifting POL's thesis — a US-Iran de-escalation that sends Brent back down would remove the tailwind just as fast as it arrived.

Holding up well technically: only 0.99% off its 20-day high despite today's -0.98% dip, RSI a neutral 55.6, above both moving averages.
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals are only 'mixed' (fair P/E 9.09); the results date is a stockanalysis estimate, not yet confirmed by the desk's own fundamentals agent, so it could slip.

catalysts.event: OGDC quarterly results (date unconfirmed, stockanalysis estimate)
SBP Monetary Policy Committee decision — hot August CPI (11.1%) makes a cut unlikely
ATRL and POL ex-dividend book closures, confirmed — POL's Rs72.5/share payout is a 9.93% yield

risks: Geopolitical: the US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz standoff is the direct driver of today's -0.96% close and the prior day's -0.29%; a further strike or retaliation would push Brent higher still and deepen the risk-off tone across the board.

Inflation/rates: August CPI at 11.1% (vs 9.2% in July, more than triple last year) has all but killed near-term SBP rate-cut hopes into the September 14 MPC — a hotter print or a hawkish surprise would hit rate-sensitive names (autos, cement, small banks) hardest.

Governance: SECP issued final notices in its Unity Foods (UNITY) unusual/insider-trading probe on 2026-09-02, tied to a separate FIA case alleging large-scale irregularities — a reminder that name-specific governance blow-ups can hit fast and hard, independent of the macro tape.
